question: A 70-year-old man comes to the physician for evaluation of worsening nocturia, fatigue, and shortness of breath on exertion. While he used to be able to walk for 15 minutes at a time, he now has to pause every 5 minutes. Recently, he has started using two pillows to avoid waking up short of breath at night. He has a history of hypertension treated with daily amlodipine and prazosin; he has difficulty adhering to his medication regimen. His pulse is 75/min, and blood pressure is 150/90 mm Hg. Physical examination shows a laterally displaced apical heartbeat and 2+ bilateral pitting edema of the lower legs. Auscultation shows an S4 gallop and fine bibasilar rales. Further evaluation is most likely to show which of the following pathophysiologic changes in this patient?

options.opc: Decrease in total peripheral vascular resistance

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "70-year-old man with worsening nocturia and fatigue" -> "possible heart failure due to fluid overload" -> "elevated left atrial pressure" -> "pulmonary congestion" -> "fine bibasilar rales" -> "S4 gallop indicates decreased compliance" -> "possible renal hypoperfusion" -> "activation of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system" -> "constriction of efferent renal arterioles" -> 85%

CHAIN: "70-year-old man with shortness of breath and edema" -> "signs of heart failure" -> "fluid retention due to decreased cardiac output" -> "activation of compensatory mechanisms" -> "increased renin release" -> "constriction of efferent renal arterioles" -> "increased glomerular filtration pressure" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Patient has difficulty adhering to medication regimen" -> "poor blood pressure control" -> "increased workload on the heart" -> "worsening heart failure symptoms" -> "fluid retention" -> "activation of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system" -> "constriction of efferent renal arterioles" -> 75%

CHAIN: "Patient presents with bilateral pitting edema" -> "indicates fluid overload" -> "likely due to heart failure" -> "increased venous pressure" -> "activation of compensatory mechanisms" -> "constriction of efferent renal arterioles" -> 80%
analysis: The patient's symptoms and examination findings suggest heart failure, likely due to left ventricular dysfunction. The presence of nocturia, fatigue, shortness of breath on exertion, and orthopnea (using two pillows) indicates fluid overload and pulmonary congestion. In heart failure, the kidneys often respond to decreased cardiac output by constricting the efferent arterioles to maintain glomerular filtration rate (GFR), which can lead to fluid retention. Therefore, the most likely pathophysiologic change in this patient would be constriction of efferent renal arterioles to preserve renal perfusion despite heart failure. Other options do not align with the clinical picture.
